item.title: Nairobi Floods Again. When Does 'Again' Become Enough?
item.description:
On the evening of Friday, March 6, the same desperate calculation played out in home after home across Mukuru kwa Njenga, Mathare, Kibera, and Pipeline — Nairobi’s densest, most flood-prone neighbourhoods: what could be saved, and what had already been lost.

By morning, twenty-three people were dead. Hundreds of vehicles had been swallowed by roads that double as rivers every rainy season. Kenya Airways diverted flights to Mombasa. The military was deployed. A city of five million had, once again, been brought to its knees by rain.

item.title: ‘Be adults’: Joe Root gets rid of England Test team’s midnight curfew
item.description:
A Shift in Approach: England’s Test Team Embraces Responsibility

Joe Root has abolished the midnight curfew for England’s Test team, signaling a significant change in approach under his leadership. The move comes after a series of incidents involving players, including Harry Brook’s altercation with a nightclub bouncer and the suspensions of Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson for breaking curfew. Root, who returns as Test captain after Stokes’ retirement, believes that curfews are ineffective in promoting responsible behavior from players.

item.title: Rangers striker Chermiti out for 'significant period of time' with ACL injury
item.description:
Rangers Striker Chermiti Sidelined by ACL Injury

Rangers striker Youssef Chermiti will be out of commission for a significant period of time after suffering an ACL injury during Sunday’s loss to Hibernian at Ibrox. The 22-year-old Chermiti, who joined the club from Everton last summer in a deal worth up to £10m, went down in the first half of the match after colliding with the pitchside boards. He was forced to leave the stadium in a boot and knee brace.

item.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
item.description:
Under Pressure: Bournemouth Faces Uncharted Territory in the Europa League

Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base stood empty, save for the lingering presence of departing head coach Andoni Iraola, as his successor Marco Rose prepared for the monumental task ahead. The new head coach has a lot to live up to after last season’s sixth-placed finish, a feat that saw the club qualify for Europe for the first time. And Iraola’s parting gift was a testament to the respect between the two coaches – a cordial farewell that belied the immense pressure now on Rose’s shoulders.

item.title: Will summit encourage Scottish clubs to give youth a chance?
item.description:
A Call to Arms for Scotland’s Senior Clubs

In a stark illustration of the dearth of opportunities for young Scottish players, Rangers’ Robbie Ure made his debut for the club at the age of 18, only to be limited to a total of three minutes of game time that season. This meager exposure ultimately led to Ure’s departure for Anderlecht in Belgium, where he has since flourished, scoring 15 goals in 15 games and attracting the attention of Sevilla.

item.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
item.description:
Liverpool’s Turbulent Summer Takes a Dramatic Turn

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) are on the cusp of a £1.35 billion deal that will see a 30% stake in the Premier League club sold to a consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. The proposed sale, which has been months in the making, would mark a significant shift in the ownership structure of the Merseyside club and inject a substantial influx of capital into the business.

item.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
item.description:
Swap Deal Unfolds: Crystal Palace and Everton Reach Agreement

Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil, marking a significant development in the transfer market. The deal comes six months after McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, publicly criticized Palace for their handling of the winger’s potential transfer to the club.

The swap deal sees McNeil, who was set to join Palace in February but saw the deal collapse due to a change in circumstances, now heading to Selhurst Park in exchange for Johnson. Both players are expected to sign four-year contracts with the option of an additional 12 months. A medical for both players is scheduled for Monday.

item.title: Rangers chairman expects up to five more signings
item.description:
Rangers’ Transfer Window Ambitions

Rangers chairman Andrew Cavenagh has expressed his expectation of up to five additional signings before the transfer window closes, despite the club’s struggling start to the season. In a meeting with shareholders, Cavenagh acknowledged that results are not meeting his expectations, with the Ibrox club having secured only one point from their two Scottish Premiership games under new manager Derek McInnes.

The club has already bolstered their squad with nine new faces this summer, but Cavenagh remains optimistic about their prospects, stating that he hopes three to five more players will join the team. This sentiment was echoed by chief executive Jim Gillespie, who described the appointment of McInnes as a deliberate effort to bring in a “Klopp-style manager” who would adopt a proactive approach to the game. Gillespie noted that McInnes had been a top target for the club for an extended period and that his style and culture align with Rangers’ vision for the future.

item.title: Hogh hits hat-trick as Celtic ease past hapless Kilmarnock
item.description:
Historic Hat-Trick Secures Celtic’s Impressive Victory

Kasper Hogh’s exceptional performance on the new grass pitch at Rugby Park propelled Celtic to a resounding 5-1 win over Kilmarnock in their Scottish Premiership encounter. The Danish striker’s first-half hat-trick, scored in the 2nd, 33rd, and 35th minutes, proved to be the decisive factor in the Hoops’ triumph.

The attendance at Rugby Park was 8,353, a testament to the enthusiasm of the home fans, who had been eagerly anticipating their team’s first match on the new grass pitch. However, their hopes were short-lived, as Hogh’s early strike, which came just 64 seconds into the game, set the tone for the rest of the match. The £11m signing nodded into an empty net after Engels’ cross, silencing his early critics and silencing any doubts about his ability.

item.title: Five-time Super League winner Makinson to retire at end of 2026 campaign
item.description:
A Legacy of Excellence: Makinson to Hang Up His Boots

Tommy Makinson has announced that he will retire from professional rugby league at the end of the 2026 Super League campaign, ending a storied career that has spanned over a decade and a half. The 34-year-old Catalans Dragons wing, whose birthday falls in October, has made a lasting impact on the sport, with a tally of five Super League titles and over 300 appearances for his former club, St Helens.

item.title: True Love seeks Prix Maurice de Gheest crown at Deauville
item.description:
Racing towards Glory: True Love Seeks Prix Maurice de Gheest Crown

True Love, the Aidan O’Brien-trained champion, is poised to take on the best of the best in the Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville on Sunday, with the Group One crown within her sights. The 1000 Guineas winner, narrowly touched off by Thesecretadversary last month in the Prix Jean Prat, has been a dominant force in the sprinting ranks, and her versatility is expected to serve her well in this challenging test.

item.title: Wales must learn from Bosnia loss in Euros bid - Rush
item.description:
Disappointing Start to the Year: Wales’ Task Becomes Increasingly Challenging

Wales’ bid to qualify for the Euro 2028 tournament hit a roadblock, as they failed to win any of their four matches so far this year. The team’s struggle to secure a spot in the summer showpiece in the USA, Canada, and Mexico culminated in a painful penalty shootout loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March. This setback has left the Welsh national side facing a daunting task in the remaining months of 2026, as they prepare to take on Portugal, Norway, and Denmark in Nations League A.

item.title: In Confirming Blanche, Senators Endorse a Justice Dept. Under Trump’s Sway
item.description:
Confirmation and Controversy

In a contentious Senate vote, lawmakers have confirmed Todd Blanche as a federal judge, sparking widespread criticism from civil rights groups and Democrats. The confirmation marks a significant escalation of the ongoing battle between the White House and Capitol Hill over the role of the Justice Department.

The Senate’s endorsement of Blanche sends a clear signal that the Trump administration’s influence over the federal judiciary will continue to expand. Blanche has been a vocal supporter of the administration’s expansive view of executive power, and has repeatedly argued that President Trump possesses a nearly limitless right to directly control the actions of the Justice Department.

item.title: Mbeumo scores in encouraging Man Utd draw with PSG but Mount injured
item.description:
Pre-Season Momentum Gains Traction as Man Utd Draw with PSG

Manchester United’s pre-season preparations continued on a positive trajectory, securing a 1-1 draw against European champions Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg, Sweden. The encouraging result, tempered only by the injury to Mason Mount, serves as a testament to the team’s growing cohesion and resilience under new management.

Bryan Mbeumo’s late equaliser, assisted by Amad Diallo, salvaged a draw that had initially seemed destined for the visitors. However, the momentum had shifted decisively in United’s favour following Diallo’s impressive display, which saw him win the ball back high up the pitch and tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish.

item.title: Ivory Coast’s ‘talking drum’ returns to home village after 110 years
item.description:
Centuries of Silence Broken

Ivory Coast’s ’talking drum’ returns to home village after 110 years

In a poignant homecoming, the Djidji Ayokwe, a sacred “talking drum” looted by French troops in 1916, has finally been returned to its ancestral home in Ivory Coast. The revered drum, which played a vital role in the Ebrie community’s communication and warning systems for generations, was formally handed over by French authorities in February, marking the end of a 110-year odyssey.

item.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
item.description:
A New Era for the Huddersfield Giants: Leaving Huddersfield Behind

The Huddersfield Giants, a Betfred Super League side, have announced their intention to relocate to Dewsbury’s Flair Stadium from the 2027 season onwards. This decision comes after a period of uncertainty, during which the club had been seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

The Giants’ move to Dewsbury is contingent upon RFL board approval, but the club has already begun investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground. The upgrade will transform the venue, increasing capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators and creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch. The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of fan concourses, significant upgrades to hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, player dressing rooms, and press facilities, elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

item.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
item.description:
Fifa’s Leadership Under Scrutiny

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has vehemently denied allegations that Uefa paid off a female employee who is said to have been in a romantic relationship with him while he was the organisation’s general secretary. The explosive claims, which surfaced in reports by The Daily Telegraph, have sent shockwaves through the world of international football.

Infantino, who served as Uefa’s general secretary from 2009 to 2016, has been at the centre of a brewing storm for several weeks, with criticism mounting over his plan to seek private investment in a company that would manage Fifa’s major competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. The Uefa president has confirmed that a “departure payment” was made to the alleged female partner, along with covering the fees for an MBA course, citing that the payment was in line with regulations in place at the time. However, Fifa has categorically dismissed the allegations as “categorically untrue,” with a spokesman for the organisation stating that any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

item.title: AFL boss Craig Drummond apologises over Geelong concussion waiver: ‘The club went too far’
item.description:
AFL Confronts Concussion Conundrum

AFL Commission chair Craig Drummond has issued a rare apology for the Geelong Football Club’s secret concussion deal with player Jake Kolodjashnij, admitting that “the club went too far” in including a waiver in the informed consent document. This development comes after a week of intense scrutiny, with the club scraping the waiver on Thursday and the AFL releasing a statement distancing itself from the agreement.

The controversy centers on a 2024 agreement between Geelong and Kolodjashnij, in which the player took on legal responsibility for any potential future head trauma. Drummond, who was Geelong’s president and on the club board at the time, acknowledged that the club’s actions were “extremely complex and sensitive,” but ultimately acknowledged that the waiver was a misstep. “Regardless of the player’s agreement, the club went too far in adding a waiver into an informed consent document, and it will be removed,” he said.

item.title: New Delhi on red alert as heavy rains pound the city
item.description:
Turbulent Skies Over the Capital

Heavy rains have brought New Delhi to a standstill, with the Indian capital’s usually congested streets transformed into murky rivers. The unprecedented downpour has left commuters stranded, and officials scrambling to mitigate the chaos.

The deluge, which began on Tuesday evening, has dumped over 300 millimeters of rain in the past 48 hours, with some areas receiving as much as 450 mm. The sheer volume of water has overwhelmed the city’s drainage system, causing widespread flooding and disrupting traffic across the metropolitan area. “We are doing everything we can to clear the roads and restore normalcy,” said a spokesperson for the Delhi Municipal Corporation. “However, with the rain showing no signs of abating, the situation remains precarious.”

item.title: Hull surges up leaderboard with course-record 62 at PIF London Championship
item.description:
Hull’s Record-Breaking Round Stuns at PIF London Championship

Charley Hull’s remarkable course record 62 has catapulted her into second place at the PIF London Championship, leaving a trail of stunned competitors in her wake. The English golfer’s blistering performance has sent shockwaves through the Ladies European Tour (LET), with many hailing her achievement as a testament to her unwavering dedication and unrelenting passion for the sport.

Hull’s second-day heroics saw her break the course record set by compatriot Georgia Hall in 2021, and her round of 11 under par has joined an elite group of LET records alongside the likes of Haeran Ryu, Jessica Korda, Alison Lee, and Karrie Webb. The five-time LET winner’s incredible display was marked by a bogey-free round, with the highlight of her day coming at the first hole, where she sunk an eagle to set the tone for an unforgettable round.

item.title: Diego Maradona bloated, bedridden and resigned before death, says masseur
item.description:
Maradona’s Descent into Isolation

Diego Maradona’s final days were marked by a profound decline in his physical and mental well-being, according to the testimony of his masseur, Nicolas Taffarel. In a court trial examining the circumstances surrounding the football icon’s death, Taffarel described a Maradona who was bedridden, resigned, and detached from the world around him.

Maradona’s condition had become increasingly dire in the days leading up to his death. Taffarel testified that the 1986 World Cup winner had become reluctant to even leave his bed, refusing to eat, wash, or attend to his personal hygiene. This precipitous decline was a stark contrast to the vibrant, larger-than-life figure that Maradona had been just a short time before. The masseur recalled that Maradona’s physical appearance had also suffered, with the football legend appearing bloated and his legs swollen.

item.title: Must-win Hossler fires 61 to lead Wyndham after day one
item.description:
Unstoppable Momentum: Hossler’s 61 Puts Him at the Top

Tom Hossler’s remarkable first round at the Wyndham Championship catapulted him to the top of the leaderboard, with a sizzling 61 that left the competition scrambling to keep pace. The American golfer’s blistering performance on day one at Sedgefield Country Club in Greensboro, North Carolina, set the tone for what promises to be a thrilling conclusion to the tournament.

Hossler’s 10-under-par 61 was a masterclass in precision and power, as he navigated the course with a mix of precision drives and clutch putts. His exceptional play was a testament to his unwavering focus and dedication to his craft. The 28-year-old golfer has been in top form all season, and this latest display has further solidified his position as a top contender for the championship title.

item.title: Norway call on Infantino to resign but Mexico & Argentina back Fifa president
item.description:
Rift Within the World’s Governing Body: Norway Calls for Infantino’s Resignation

Norway’s football association has taken a bold step by calling for the resignation of Gianni Infantino, the 56-year-old president of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (Fifa), amidst controversy surrounding his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. This move comes as a significant escalation of pressure on Infantino, following withdrawals of support from several football associations, including England, Wales, Croatia, and Albania.

item.title: Who will exit Chelsea? How Blues could cut 41-man squad
item.description:
Chelsea Confronts Crisis of Excess: The Battle to Trim a 41-Man Squad

Chelsea’s new manager, Xabi Alonso, is facing a daunting task: whittling down a bloated squad of 41 senior players to a more manageable 25. The consequences of inaction are stark, with the Premier League’s 25-man squad rule looming large. The club’s precarious financial situation, tied to a Uefa settlement agreement, demands drastic action.

Chelsea’s reliance on a large squad, a legacy of their past successes, has been compounded by their recent failure to qualify for European competition. The absence of continental football has left them with an unwieldy collection of players, some of whom are not involved in the first team. Alonso knows that the situation cannot persist, as it would only serve to undermine squad harmony and create tensions among the players.

item.title: Trump administration to pay €1.06 billion to cancel RWE offshore wind leases
item.description:
Billions Paid to Cancel Offshore Wind Leases: A Setback for Renewable Energy

The Trump administration has agreed to pay a staggering €1.06 billion to German energy firm RWE to cancel the company’s offshore wind leases off the coasts of New York, California, and Louisiana. This move comes as part of a broader campaign by President Donald Trump to halt wind energy projects across the US, with him repeatedly dismissing wind turbines as unsightly and labeling them an “economic and environmental disaster.”

item.title: South Korea police raid football association over Hong appointment process
item.description:
Investigation into Football Association Deepens as Police Raid Offices

South Korean police have carried out a raid on the offices of the Korea Football Association (KFA) as part of an investigation into the appointment process of former coach Hong Myung-bo. The move follows a parliamentary inquiry into the matter, with lawmakers questioning whether Hong received special treatment in his reappointment to the role.

Hong, a veteran coach, returned to the national team in 2024 after a previous stint from 2013 to 2014. His appointment was the subject of controversy when it emerged that the KFA had abandoned a months-long search for a foreign coach and instead appointed him following a brief meeting. The decision was seen as unusual, given the extensive search process that had been undertaken.

item.title: Bethell to miss Pakistan Test series as Pope recalled
item.description:
England’s New Era

Joe Root’s second stint as England Test captain begins with a three-match series against Pakistan, starting in Leeds on August 19. The team, seeking to turn the page on a difficult spell on and off the field, has undergone significant changes. Notably, Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse have been recalled to the squad for the first time since the disastrous Ashes tour of Australia last winter.

However, another key player, Jacob Bethell, will miss the entirety of the series due to a knee injury sustained during England’s ODI series against India in July. This setback has led to the inclusion of Essex wicketkeeper Jordan Cox at No 3, who made his Test debut earlier this summer. Cox’s promotion highlights the need for fresh talent to bolster England’s batting lineup.

item.title: Could the Iran war derail Donald Trump’s legacy?
item.description:
War and Legacy

President Trump is seeking to reframe the Iran war, a move likely to be closely scrutinized by voters as the 2026 midterm elections approach in November. Trump has long been a vocal supporter of military action against Iran, but recent developments have shifted the spotlight onto the war’s potential impact on his legacy.

The Iran war has been a contentious issue throughout Trump’s presidency, with many Democrats and some Republicans voicing opposition to the conflict. As the war continues to drag on, Trump appears to be recalibrating his stance, acknowledging that the war’s unpopularity may have significant implications for his party in the upcoming elections. The president has signaled that he is open to revising his approach to the conflict, potentially seeking a path towards de-escalation or even a negotiated settlement.

item.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
item.description:
A Shift in the Political Landscape

Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York has hailed Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s narrow victory in the Michigan Senate primary as a significant breakthrough, suggesting that the progressive candidate’s win demonstrates his ability to connect with working-class voters.

El-Sayed’s margin of victory was less than 2 percentage points, marking a closely contested race in which the progressive candidate’s grassroots campaign and appeal to voters on issues such as healthcare and economic justice proved decisive. The outcome is being seen by many as a testament to El-Sayed’s ability to transcend the conventional categorizations of politics, as Mayor Mamdani observed in his comments on the matter.

item.title: Players hit out at A-Leagues’ conduct over pay offer: ‘Continues to erode trust’
item.description:
A-League Negotiations Stall Amid Allegations of Bad Faith

Players in the Australian Professional Leagues (APL) have expressed disappointment and frustration with the A-League’s latest pay offer, which was hastily taken to the media just hours after it was sent to the Professional Footballers Australia (PFA). The move has been criticized for eroding trust between the players and the league, with PFA chief executive Beau Busch accusing the APL of negotiating in bad faith.

item.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
item.description:
The Progressive Paradox: El-Sayed’s Historic Victory in Michigan Sets the Stage for a Crucial Test of Left-Wing Politics

Abdul El-Sayed’s decisive win in the Michigan Senate primary marks a watershed moment in the state’s electoral landscape, as the 37-year-old physician-turned-politician now faces the daunting task of appealing to a broader electorate in the general election. El-Sayed’s unapologetically liberal platform, which has resonated with the state’s progressive base, will be put to the ultimate test in a contest against a well-established incumbent or a seasoned Republican challenger. The implications of this outcome are far-reaching, as El-Sayed’s candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate with unabashedly liberal positions win a general election in a moderate state?

item.title: UN rights chief says Iran executed at least 56 people since March
item.description:
Execution Surge in Iran: UN Rights Chief Sounds Alarm

At least 56 people have been executed in Iran on national security-related charges since March 19, including 27 in cases linked to nationwide protests at the start of the year, according to United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk. This alarming rise in capital punishment is a stark indication of the Iranian government’s willingness to use state-sanctioned executions to crush public opposition.

item.title: Israeli Strikes May Undermine Trump’s Peace Plan for Gaza
item.description:
Uncertain Peace Prospects

Israeli Strikes May Undermine Trump’s Peace Plan for Gaza

President Trump’s long-awaited peace plan for Gaza, which envisioned a phased Israeli withdrawal and disarmament of Hamas, has been thrown into jeopardy by a recent escalation of violence. Israel’s military launched a series of strikes against Hamas targets in the Palestinian enclave, casting doubt on the viability of the US initiative.

According to reports, the Israeli military has intensified its attacks on Hamas strongholds in Gaza, leading to a significant increase in casualties and displacement among Palestinian civilians. This marked escalation has raised alarm among international observers, who had been cautiously optimistic about the prospects for peace in the region under the Trump administration’s proposed framework.

item.title: Scarlets chief Daniels dismisses Ospreys merger
item.description:
Uncertainty Looms Over Welsh Rugby’s Future

Scarlets managing director Jon Daniels has issued a stark warning to the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) over its plans to cut the number of professional teams from four to three by 2028, stating that the governing body must provide greater transparency and justification for its decision. The announcement has left Scarlets and Ospreys in a state of uncertainty, with the west licence either being awarded to the Llanelli-based side or the Swansea-based rivals.

item.title: Why Arsenal are signing Newcastle captain Guimaraes
item.description:
Building a Winning Midfield: Arsenal’s Ambitious Move for Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has made clear that the club must be ambitious to build on their Premier League title win, and the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes is a significant step towards achieving that aim. The 28-year-old Brazilian midfielder will join a new-look Arsenal midfield, bringing with him a wealth of Premier League experience and a proven track record of success.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur battled relegation last season, but a busy summer transfer window could see the London club back in competitive form under Roberto De Zerbi - Tottenham Hotspur 2026-27 season preview
item.description:
Rebuilding Momentum

Tottenham Hotspur’s rollercoaster ride last season ended on a note of relief, with a last-day victory securing their Premier League status. The harsh reality was that it took a dramatic finale to salvage their campaign, which had been marred by inconsistency and a series of disappointing results. However, with a new season on the horizon, the London club is poised to bounce back under the guidance of Roberto De Zerbi, the Italian manager who masterminded a remarkable turnaround.

item.title: Quiz! Can you name every team to have won one of English football's top four tiers?
item.description:
A Legacy of Excellence: Unpacking the Rich History of English Football’s Top Four Tiers

In a testament to the enduring appeal of the beautiful game, a staggering 95 teams have claimed victory in one of English football’s top four tiers over nearly 140 years of history. This milestone is a reflection of the country’s rich sporting heritage, one that has been shaped by generations of passionate players, dedicated coaches, and devoted fans. From the early days of professional football to the present era of the Premier League and EFL, the top four divisions have been the stage upon which some of the greatest teams and players in English football history have etched their names.

item.title: Todd Blanche Clears Committee Vote, Paving Way for Attorney General Confirmation
item.description:
Committee Approval Sets Stage for Attorney General Confirmation

Todd Blanche’s nomination for Attorney General has cleared the committee hurdle, with a vote that paves the way for a Senate confirmation that is all but assured. The nomination now advances to the Senate floor, where Blanche is expected to secure the necessary votes, despite some lingering uncertainty among Republicans.

The committee vote, which took place earlier this week, came after several weeks of intense scrutiny of Blanche’s qualifications and background. Although several Republicans have not yet committed to supporting him, the prevailing sentiment among lawmakers suggests that Blanche will ultimately prevail. The confirmation process is expected to be a formality, with Democrats and Republicans alike acknowledging that Blanche’s nomination has broad support.

item.title: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
item.description:
Unsettling Silence Erupts in Glasgow

Several athletes have been reported missing after the conclusion of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, sparking a search effort by Police Scotland. According to reports from Uganda, four members of the country’s boxing team failed to rejoin their delegation before the scheduled return to Uganda on Tuesday. The disappearance has cast a shadow over the successful hosting of the Games, which drew nearly 3,000 athletes from 74 nations.

item.title: What to Watch in Washington State’s Primaries as Gluesenkamp Perez Faces a Challenge
item.description:
A Tense Primary Season Unfolds in Washington State

Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, the moderate Democrat who has represented Washington State’s 3rd Congressional District since 2022, finds herself in an unenviable position as she navigates the state’s primary season. According to recent reports, Gluesenkamp Perez faces challenges not only from more conservative candidates but also from those on her left flank, a development that may test her ability to hold onto the seat in the general election.

item.title: Barcelona sign Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for club-record £1.25m
item.description:
A Record-Breaking Transfer: Barcelona Sign Kerolin for £1.25m

Barcelona have made a major coup in the transfer market, securing the services of Brazil forward Kerolin from Manchester City for a club-record £1.25m. The signing is a significant statement of intent from the defending European champions, who are understood to believe Kerolin has the pace and trickery on the ball to become a regular goalscorer in the Champions League.

The transfer fee eclipses Olivia Smith’s £1m move to Arsenal in 2025 and Melvine Malard’s £850,000 switch from Manchester United to Chelsea, making it the largest sum received for a sale by a Women’s Super League side. Kerolin, 26, was part of the City side that won the WSL title and the Women’s FA Cup last season, and was with the club for 18 months after arriving from North Carolina Courage in January 2025.

item.title: Nine killed in escalating long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine
item.description:
Escalating Conflict: Russia and Ukraine Trade Heavy Blows

At least nine people have been killed in a series of long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine, with civilians bearing the brunt of the escalating violence. The attacks have targeted warehouses, oil refineries, and residential areas, resulting in a mounting toll of non-combatant casualties on both sides.

The strikes have been characterised by their precision and scope, with Ukrainian drones and Russian missiles hitting critical infrastructure and civilian targets. In one incident, a Ukrainian drone struck a warehouse in the Moscow region, killing five people and injuring 10. Regional Governor Andrei Vorobyov confirmed the attack, which was one of three overnight attacks on warehouses across Russia. Another warehouse belonging to e-commerce giant Wildberries was also struck by drones in the Tver region, northwest of Moscow, sparking a blaze.

item.title: UFC’s Allan Nascimento dead aged 34 after apparent heart attack
item.description:
A Fallen Fighter: The Sudden Passing of UFC’s Allan Nascimento

In a devastating turn of events, the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) has announced the untimely death of 34-year-old fighter Allan Nascimento, who suffered an apparent heart attack in his sleep. The news, confirmed by the UFC late Monday, has sent shockwaves throughout the mixed martial arts community, leaving friends, family, and fans reeling in grief.

Nascimento, a respected flyweight competitor, last took to the Octagon in June, suffering a split decision loss to Mitch Raposo. Despite his recent defeat, the Brazilian fighter remained a beloved figure in the MMA world, known for his determination, humility, and unwavering commitment to his craft. As a member of the renowned Chute Boxe gym in Brazil, Nascimento had amassed a UFC record of four wins and two defeats, with a remarkable overall MMA record of 22 wins and seven defeats.

item.title: Record number of new managers for season like no other
item.description:
A New Era for English Football

Married couple Nixon Giovanni Paz and his wife were found bound and shot dead in Guatemala, a country they were forcibly deported to by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last year. The gruesome discovery has sparked outrage and calls for reform in the US immigration system.

However, their tragic fate has raised questions about the consequences of such policies and the vulnerabilities of deportees in foreign countries.

item.description:

item.title: Celtic complete club-record signing of striker Hogh
item.description:
Celtic’s Statement Signing: Hogh’s Arrival Sparks Hope and Questions

item.title: AIG Women's Open: Full R1 groupings and Royal Lytham tee times
item.description:
Tee Times Set for AIG Women’s Open, Defending Champion Miyu Yamashita Aims for Second Consecutive Title

The 50th AIG Women’s Open tees off at Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in Lancashire on Thursday, with 144 players competing in the final women’s major of the year. Defending champion Miyu Yamashita returns, seeking to become the first back-to-back winner since Yani Tseng. Yamashita will be out in the late-early wave alongside world No 2 Jeeno Thitikul and Lauren Coughlin.

item.title: Malaysia detains more than 100 Rohingya seeking help from the UN
item.description:
Rohingya Refugees Detained in Malaysia: Humanitarian Consequences of Rising Xenophobia

Malaysian authorities have apprehended over 100 Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers who were attempting to seek assistance from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in response to mounting persecution in the country. The mass detention is a stark illustration of the escalating tensions and discriminatory attitudes faced by this vulnerable group within Malaysian society.

The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority from Myanmar, have been subjected to intense harassment and intimidation in Malaysia. A surge in online hate speech and misinformation has further exacerbated their predicament, with many reports of physical and verbal abuse. In the face of such adversity, the detained individuals, including women and children, had sought refuge at the UNHCR’s offices in a desperate bid for protection and recognition.

item.title: Trump asks US Supreme Court to allow mail-in voting restrictions
item.description:
Trump Seeks Supreme Court Intervention in Mail-In Voting Dispute

The administration of President Donald Trump has submitted an emergency request to the US Supreme Court, seeking to lift a lower court’s ruling that blocked key provisions of Trump’s executive order restricting mail-in voting in 23 Democratic-led states and Washington, DC.

The move comes as the midterm elections approach, with the outcome set to determine control of the US House of Representatives and Senate. Trump’s executive order, issued in March, aimed to reshape the US electoral landscape by imposing sweeping restrictions on mail-in voting, which has been a cornerstone of Democratic voter outreach efforts.

item.title: Rose Davies storms home to win Australia’s first Commonwealth Games athletics gold
item.description:
Australia Seizes the Spotlight at Commonwealth Games with Historic Athletics Gold

Rose Davies stormed to victory in the women’s 10,000m event, securing Australia’s first athletics gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 26-year-old from New South Wales kicked away from Kenya’s Diana Wanza in the final kilometre, crossing the finish line 10 seconds ahead of her closest rival.

Davies’ triumph marked a significant milestone for Australian athletics, with the country’s first gold medal in the women’s 10,000m event. The Novocastrian, who holds national records in both the 5,000m and 10,000m distances, attributed her success to her consistent training and growth as a runner.

item.title: 'Medal dream didn't come true but my other dream is fighting brain cancer'
item.description:
A Triumph of the Human Spirit

Scotland’s Archie Goodburn walked out to a thunderous ovation at Tollcross International Swimming Centre on Monday, his heart racing with anticipation. The 25-year-old swimmer had qualified for the Commonwealth Games final just 24 hours prior, a feat that would have seemed impossible given his circumstances. Goodburn had been diagnosed with brain cancer two years ago, at the age of 22, and was told he might not see his 40s.

item.title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Allow Order Restricting Mail Voting
item.description:
The High Court Intervention

The Trump administration has filed a request with the Supreme Court to stay an appeals court ruling that blocked key provisions of a mail-in voting executive order. The move marks a significant escalation in the administration’s efforts to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

At the heart of the controversy lies a contentious executive order issued by President Trump in the wake of the 2020 presidential election. The order, which aimed to restrict mail-in voting in several states, was met with swift opposition from state election officials and civil rights groups. When an appeals court ultimately blocked key parts of the order, the Trump administration saw an opportunity to take its case to the nation’s highest court.

item.title: Has Burnham kept his promise to do better on Israel’s war on Gaza?
item.description:
The Uneasy Legacy of a Broken Promise

Britain’s new cabinet has sparked a flurry of speculation about the country’s stance on Israel’s war on Gaza, but at the heart of the debate lies a question: has Prime Minister Rishi Sunak’s predecessor, Liz Truss, been kept accountable for her predecessor’s pledge to do better on the issue?

On assuming office, Prime Minister Truss’s government faced intense scrutiny over its predecessor’s record on supporting Israel. As part of a broader effort to rebrand Britain’s foreign policy, Boris Johnson’s administration had promised to “do better” on the conflict, amid mounting criticism that the UK’s previous stance had been overly sympathetic to Israel. Yet, despite the rhetoric, the Johnson government’s actions on the ground did little to change the status quo.

item.title: Sabalenka & Djokovic to team up in US Open mixed doubles
item.description:
Star Power Dominates US Open Mixed Doubles Lineup

Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka are set to team up in the US Open mixed doubles, a move that has drawn significant attention and interest in the revamped event. item.title: Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offer
item.description:
Manchester City’s Rodri Saga Takes a New Turn

Manchester City’s hopes for Rodri to sign a new deal have been complicated by Real Madrid’s interest in the midfielder. The Spanish club has revised its stance on Rodri following his impressive displays as captain of Spain’s World Cup-winning team, where he won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player.

Rodri’s contract at Manchester City expires in June 2027, and despite the club’s optimism about negotiations, Real Madrid is now understood to be preparing a bid. This development may prompt interest from other elite clubs, including Barcelona, which could move for Rodri after Frenkie de Jong’s medial collateral ligament injury ruled him out for months. Paris Saint-Germain, too, is known to admire Rodri.

item.title: Identical Roper twins win gymnastics bronze medals
item.description:
Commonwealth Games 2026: Identical Twins Make History in Gymnastics

In a breathtaking display of skill and determination, the Roper twins, Abigail and Emily, have etched their names into Welsh team history, each claiming a bronze medal in the Commonwealth Games gymnastics events. The identical siblings achieved this remarkable feat within a span of just a few hours, leaving their fans and fellow competitors alike in awe.

The first Roper twin to claim a medal was Abigail, who secured third place in the women’s vault event. This achievement not only marked a personal milestone for Abigail but also set the tone for her sister’s subsequent success. Emily, who had initially finished fourth in the vault, demonstrated remarkable resilience in bouncing back to capture a bronze medal in the uneven bars event.

item.title: Chiesa happy but wants new chapter at Liverpool
item.description:
A Divided Mindset: Chiesa’s Liverpool Dilemma

Federico Chiesa’s latest remarks have reignited speculation about his future at Liverpool, despite the Italian forward’s insistence that he is solely focused on the Reds. In a candid interview with reporters following Saturday’s friendly against Sunderland, Chiesa stated that he is “happy” at Anfield, but his assertion is tempered by the reality of his limited playing time and scoring record under Arne Slot.

Over two seasons, Chiesa has started just one Premier League game and managed only five goals in 50 appearances across all competitions. The 28-year-old, who joined Liverpool from Juventus in a £12.5m deal in 2024, has been a subject of discussion regarding his consistency in the Premier League. In June, Chiesa told La Gazzetta dello Sport that if he fails to find his footing in the league, he would consider looking elsewhere. This admission has been viewed by some as a veiled threat to his current employers.

item.title: Malaysia to host rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race in October
item.description:

Malaysia’s Sepang circuit will host a rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, marking a significant development in the Formula One calendar. The Liberty Media-owned sport announced the news on Sunday, with Formula One Chief Executive Stefano Domenicali revealing that an agreement had been signed between the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain, as well as the governing FIA and Formula One.

item.title: Trump Seems Trapped by Iran War, Even as He Wields the World’s Biggest Hammer
item.description:
The Unyielding Constraint

Donald Trump, the 45th President of the United States, has found himself increasingly entangled in a conflict with Iran, a predicament he seemed to believe would be easily won. item.title: England 'far off their best' in netball defeat to Australia in Glasgow
item.description:
Disappointing Display

England’s Vitality Roses suffered their first defeat of the Commonwealth Games on Sunday, succumbing to a 66-47 loss against reigning champions Australia in Glasgow.

The Vitality Roses trailed 18-11 after the first quarter and 35-24 at half-time before a series of handling errors helped Australia stretch their lead to 56-35 with 15 minutes left. Despite managing to win the final quarter 12-10, England were unable to salvage the game, allowing Australia to claim a convincing victory. Olivia Tchine was England’s top scorer with 23 goals, but her efforts were not enough to prevent the defeat.

item.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Ramsay-Peaty bounces back, Australia beat England in netball, and more on day three – live
item.description:
Commonwealth Comeback: Australia Dominates Netball, Gymnasts Shine on Day Three

The win marks a significant comeback for the Australian side, which had been pushed to its limits in earlier matches. Ramsay-Peaty’s impressive performance was instrumental in the team’s triumph, with her skill and strategy on court proving decisive.

Meanwhile, in the men’s 60kg weightlifting event, Bin Kasdan Mohamad Aniq of Malaysia has taken the gold, setting a new Commonwealth Games record with a lift of 152kg in the clean. Rishikanta Singh Chanambam of India secured silver with a new Games record of 121kg in the snatch, while Joshua Amunga Mboya of Kenya earned bronze.

item.title: Israeli forces target Gaza’s Al-Aqsa hospital
item.description:
Chaos in the Holy City

The streets of Jerusalem’s Old City remained eerily quiet yesterday evening, as news of the devastating strike on Al-Aqsa hospital sent shockwaves through the Israeli-Palestinian community. The incident has sparked widespread outrage, with many calling for an end to the military campaign in Gaza.

item.title: Liverpool start Iraola era in style to beat Sunderland but Gomez injury deepens defensive worries
item.description:
A Promising Start, but Defensive Concerns Linger for Liverpool

A 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville marked the beginning of the Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool, but the new head coach’s first game was marred by a worrying injury to Joe Gomez, which left the team’s central defensive options looking alarmingly thin.

The game itself was a comfortable win for Liverpool, with second-half finishes from Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa, and Lewis Koumas delivering a decisive blow to Sunderland’s hopes. The Liverpool players who took to the field in Nashville showed promising signs, with lively displays from Calum Scanlon, Kieran Morrison, and Koumas catching Iraola’s eye.

item.title: Inside the Rushed Effort to Get Trump His New Air Force One
item.description:
The High-Stakes Gamble on Trump’s New Air Force One

As the United States Air Force scrambles to meet an ambitious deadline for the delivery of a new Air Force One, the project’s expedited timeline has come at a steep price: ballooning costs and compromises on critical safety features. According to a comprehensive investigation by The New York Times, President Trump’s personal drive to accelerate the aircraft’s development has put the program’s integrity at risk.

item.title: The Global South is being forced to choose creditors over children
item.description:
The Devouring Debt

The world’s most vulnerable populations are facing a stark choice: creditors or children. As the financial system dictates that governments prioritize debt service over education, the consequences are dire. In 113 countries with a total population of 6.1 billion, governments now spend more on servicing debt than educating their people. The data, released by UNESCO, reveals a stark hierarchy where creditors hold sway over children.

In low-income countries, debt payments are nearly four times education expenditure. For 18 of the most heavily indebted nations, governments spend at least five times more on debt than on education. These are not merely signs of strained public finances, but a reflection of the international financial order that severely restricts governments’ choices.

item.title: Norris puts upgraded McLaren on top from Hamilton in final practice
item.description:
McLaren’s Resurgence: Norris Puts Upgraded Car on Top

The tenuous grip on pole position held by Ferrari and Mercedes appears to be slipping, as Lando Norris’s remarkable display in final practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix has catapulted McLaren into contention. item.title: At Correspondents’ Dinner, a Rambling Trump Hurls Insults
item.description:
Eclipsing Decorum

At a gala where the nation’s press corps typically comes together to poke fun at itself, President Trump hijacked the Correspondents’ Dinner with a rambling, vitriolic address that left the audience in stunned silence.

The annual event, a long-standing tradition of levity and camaraderie between journalists and the administration, has been strained in recent years. Relations between President Trump and the press have been contentious, with the President frequently deriding the media as “fake news” and “enemies of the people.” This year’s dinner was no exception. President Trump, despite being the guest of honor, used his keynote speech to launch a scathing attack on the press, veering wildly off-script and departing from the evening’s lighthearted tone.

item.title: Premier League: club-by-club guide to transfer business so far – and what they still need
item.description:
Transfer Tectonics: A Summer of Movement in the Premier League

As the English transfer record continues to be shattered, with Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers making their moves, the Premier League is witnessing a summer of unprecedented activity. item.title: Waratahs spoil Fijian Drua party to claim third straight Super Rugby Women’s title
item.description:
A Title to Remember

In the sweltering heat of Ba, Fiji, the NSW Waratahs etched their names in history books with a resounding 34-17 victory over Fijian Drua in the grand final of the Super Rugby Women’s tournament. item.title: Israeli settlers escalate attacks on Palestinians near Nablus
item.description:
Unrest Ignites in the West Bank

Tensions have reached a boiling point in the West Bank, as Israeli settlers have escalated their attacks on Palestinian communities near Nablus. The most recent wave of violence has seen numerous homes and vehicles set ablaze, exacerbating an already volatile situation.

In the past few days, a series of coordinated attacks has ravaged the Palestinian villages of Jalud and Yasuf, leaving residents reeling in fear. According to eyewitness accounts, groups of settlers, estimated to be in the dozens, descended upon the villages, targeting homes and properties with fire. Local authorities have confirmed at least 12 structures have been damaged or destroyed, with many more reported to be at risk of being torched.

item.title: Van Veen edges past Wade to book Price SF showdown in Blackpool
item.description:
A Thrilling Turn of Events in Blackpool

In a contest that ebbed and flowed like a tempestuous sea, Gian van Veen edged past James Wade to book a semi-final showdown with Gerwyn Price at the World Matchplay Darts, being held at the iconic Winter Gardens in Blackpool. The Dutchman’s 16-13 victory saw him reach the last four for the first time, setting up a tantalizing encounter with the world No 3, who recovered from a 12-8 lead to rattle off four consecutive legs and reach his first semi-final at the World Matchplay since 2022.

item.title: Hamilton fastest as Ferrari dominate Hungarian GP practice
item.description:

Lewis Hamilton’s impressive turnaround in the second practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix has left Ferrari as the clear favourites for the weekend’s crucial qualifying session. The seven-time world champion edged his team-mate Charles Leclerc to the fastest time, reversing a half-second deficit from the opening session into a 0.158s advantage.

The Italian team’s impressive one-two finish in the more representative afternoon session was a testament to their car’s adaptability and pace. Ferrari’s dominance was not merely expected, given the circuit’s unique characteristics, but the extent of their superiority has sent a clear message to their rivals. item.title: Chris Mason: What his first week in power tells us about Andy Burnham

In the whirlwind first week of Andy Burnham’s premiership, the Labour leader has sought to establish himself as a dynamic force in British politics. item.title: ‘Football can change a country’: Klopp sets sights high after unveiling as Germany head coach
item.description:
A New Era for German Football

Jürgen Klopp’s appointment as Germany’s head coach marks a significant turning point for the national team, one that promises to shake up the country’s football landscape. Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Klopp laid out his ambitious vision: to transform a fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, and to galvanize the wider community through the power of football.

For Klopp, the stakes are high. As he acknowledged, Germany’s performance in recent years has been underwhelming, with the team failing to make it past the last 16 since their 2014 World Cup victory. The 59-year-old coach, who has spent the past two years as head of global soccer for Red Bull, believes that football has the ability to unite a nation, and he is determined to prove it.

item.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
item.description:
A Foul Reaction

Sunday’s World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium will be remembered for many reasons, but the actions of Argentina players in the aftermath of Spain’s victory have left a sour taste. The incidents, which were captured on camera and widely shared on social media, saw Argentina’s Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes attack Rodri and Eric García, respectively. item.title: Gina Rinehart offers bonuses for Australian swimming medals as funding gap exposed

item.title: Burnham pauses early prison release scheme

England’s Bronze Medal Bonanza: Saka’s Hat-Trick Seals Third Place in Thrilling 10-Goal Finish

The Hard Rock Stadium in Miami erupted in a frenzy of noise and color as England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966, claiming the bronze medal with a 6-4 win over France in a 10-goal thriller. Bukayo Saka’s masterclass performance, including a hat-trick, was the catalyst for the Three Lions’ dramatic victory, which will be etched in the memories of football fans worldwide for years to come.

item.title: Latest Precipitation Models Still Seem to Underestimate Risk as ‘1,000-Year’ Rain Events Pummel Texas
item.description:
The Shifting Ground Beneath Our Feet: Texas Floods Highlight Inadequate Precipitation Models

Torrential downpours have ravaged parts of South Texas, leaving a trail of destruction and raising crucial questions about the accuracy of precipitation models. In just two years, the region has experienced not one but two major flooding disasters, with four-day rainfall totals in the towns of Uvalde and Sabinal setting records and ranking as 1,000-year rain events. These models, used to inform design criteria in local building codes, appear to be underestimating risk, according to experts.

item.title: World Cup Final Drives Billions in Bets on Kalshi and Polymarket
item.description:
The World Cup’s Dark Horse: Kalshi and Polymarket Profit from Record-Breaking Bets

The stadium was electric as Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappé clashed in the World Cup final, but the real winners may not have been the teams themselves. According to reports, the soccer tournament has driven billions of dollars in bets on prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket, propelling them to new user records and creating what may be the largest gambling event in history.

item.title: The Evolution of Presidential Travel: Horse Carriages to Air Force One
item.description:
A Symbol of Power in Motion: The Evolution of Presidential Travel

As the United States marks its 250th anniversary of presidential travel, the images of horse-drawn carriages, steam locomotives, and sleek Air Force One aircraft evoke a sense of nostalgia and awe. The evolution of presidential transportation is a testament to the country’s progress and a reflection of the office itself. From the humble beginnings of horse-drawn coaches to the high-tech marvels of today, the mode of transportation has played a crucial role in projecting an image of America to the world.

item.title: Poultry sector growth plan risks UK national security, campaigners warn
item.description:
The Poultry Sector’s Double-Edged Sword: National Security and Climate Consequences

Campaigners have sounded the alarm on the UK government’s proposed poultry sector growth plan, warning that it poses a significant threat to national security. The initiative, aimed at enhancing food security, has been met with criticism from environmental groups and experts who argue that intensive poultry farming is unsustainable and vulnerable to supply chain shocks.

At the heart of the controversy lies the government’s reliance on animal feed imports, with soy from South America accounting for 18% of the UK’s animal feed production. This reliance not only contributes to the destruction of the Amazon rainforest but also leaves the country exposed to potential supply chain disruptions. Maya Pardo, campaign lead at Communities Against Factory Farming (CAFF), emphasizes that the government’s own national security assessment highlights the risks associated with this approach.

item.title: Without Platner, Maine Democrats Scramble to Keep Grassroots Energy Alive
item.description:
Grassroots Momentum in Jeopardy

In the wake of Graham Platner’s Senate campaign collapse, Maine Democrats are scrambling to maintain the grassroots energy that had propelled him to the forefront of the party’s progressive wing. Platner’s campaign, which had gained traction among working-class voters and environmental activists, had been seen as a beacon of hope for a party desperate to break its losing streak in the state.

The activists who had rallied behind Platner are now faced with a daunting task: finding a candidate who can carry the populist message that Platner had championed. Platner’s supporters had been drawn to his unapologetic stance on issues like labor rights, affordable healthcare, and climate action. His ability to connect with ordinary Mainers had been a key factor in his campaign’s early success.

item.title: Argentina’s New York fans share hopes before 2026 World Cup final
item.description:
A World United in Passion: Argentina’s New York Fans Share Hopes Before the 2026 World Cup Final

In the heart of New York City, a vibrant tapestry of cultures has long been woven together by the threads of football. As the 2026 World Cup final approaches, the neighbourhood of Elmhurst, Queens, is swelling with excitement, its streets painted in the iconic colours of Argentina. Among the revellers are lifelong residents and descendants of the original Argentinian diaspora who settled in New York City during the tumultuous 1970s.

item.title: As Natural Disasters Expand, a Disaster-Tracking App Is Booming
item.description:
A Beacon of Hope in a Time of Crisis

In the midst of unprecedented natural disasters, a small startup has emerged as a shining example of innovation and resilience. Watch Duty, the disaster-tracking app that has long been a staple for Californians navigating the state’s increasingly volatile wildfire season, is expanding its mission to support millions of people worldwide. As the frequency and severity of natural disasters continue to rise, Watch Duty’s growth serves as a testament to the human spirit’s capacity to adapt and respond to the challenges posed by climate change.

item.title: Messi and Brady on 'prophetic' Lamine Yamal photos
item.description:
A Fateful Encounter: Messi and Brady Ponder the Prophetic Photos

Lionel Messi and Tom Brady are two of the most accomplished athletes of their respective generations, and yet, their paths converged in a moment that has been described as “very prophetic” by the NFL legend. The two sports icons gathered in New York, mere days before the World Cup final, to discuss a photograph that has taken on a life of its own – a snap from 2007 that captured Messi holding five-month-old Lamine Yamal, the current Spain captain.

item.title: E.U. Proposes Changes to Emissions Trading System
item.description:
Climate Change Fallout: E.U. Faces Backlash Over Emissions Trading System

As the European Union grapples with the daunting task of slashing greenhouse gas emissions, a new proposal to revamp the Emissions Trading System (ETS) has sparked a heated debate, threatening to disrupt the very fabric of the region’s economy. The ETS, a cornerstone of the E.U.’s climate policy, has been instrumental in reducing carbon emissions from industries such as power generation and heavy manufacturing. However, with emissions cuts becoming increasingly harder and more costly, the E.U. is now facing a green backlash from industries and communities whose livelihoods depend on the status quo.

item.title: NFL players want more grass fields after World Cup
item.description:
A Pitch for Better Turf

The NFL may be the most popular sports league in the United States, but its stadiums are not always equipped with the best playing surfaces. In a bold move, NFL players have launched a social media campaign to pressure their owners and the league to install more permanent grass fields. item.description:

item.description:

The stage is set for a highly anticipated World Cup final between Argentina and Spain, with the two teams facing off on Sunday at 3pm ET. item.title: Cyclospora Investigation Turns to Farms in Mexico
item.description:
Contaminated Produce: Unpacking the Investigation into Cyclospora Outbreaks

The United States Food and Drug Administration (F.D.A.) has announced its intention to inspect a clutch of farms in Mexico and a lettuce shredding facility in the country, in a bid to unravel the mystery behind the cyclospora contamination of lettuce supplied to a major fast-food chain. The development follows the revelation that at least 12 individuals in the United States had contracted the parasitic infection after consuming the tainted produce, sparking concerns over food safety protocols in the supply chain.

item.title: Climate Change Contributes to a Smokier World
item.description:
A World on Fire: The Unrelenting Consequences of Climate Change

As the sun sets over parched landscapes, a sinister haze spreads, shrouding the air in a toxic veil of smoke and ash. The once-clear skies of North America have become a distant memory, replaced by a perpetual twilight that threatens to choke the life out of the continent. The culprit behind this apocalyptic scenario is none other than climate change, a remorseless force that is igniting wildfires across the continent, extending the summer fire season, and leaving a trail of devastation in its wake.

item.title: Taylor Farms to Remove Products After Lettuce Is Linked to Cyclospora Cases
item.description:
Contamination Concerns Spread Beyond Borders

Taylor Farms, a major producer of leafy greens, has announced it will remove products from store shelves and recall contaminated produce after an association with cyclospora cases was identified. The move follows a growing number of reported illnesses linked to the company’s lettuce in the United States and beyond.

Taylor Farms operates in over 12 states across the country, as well as in Mexico and Canada, where its produce is distributed to various customers. Some of its contaminated lettuce ultimately ended up on the menu at Taco Bell, a popular fast-food chain. This development has sparked concerns about the potential reach and impact of the contamination, as well as the company’s efforts to mitigate the situation.

item.title: Big Tech Firms Like Oracle Turn to Bonds to Finance A.I. Data Centers
item.description:
The New Normal in Tech Financing: A.I. Data Centers Come at a Steep Price

As the global economy grapples with the far-reaching implications of artificial intelligence, a quiet revolution is unfolding in the world of big tech financing. Oracle, the corporate giant founded by Larry Ellison, has been at the forefront of this shift, using its vast wealth to fuel an unprecedented spending spree on A.I. data centers. But this financial juggernaut comes with a steep price: Oracle’s debt rating has been downgraded to just one notch above junk bond status, and the company’s stock market value has taken a significant hit.

item.title: China's Moonshot AI claims Kimi K3 can rival OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description:

item.title: West Ham captain Bowen to stay at club
item.description:

Jarrod Bowen, 29, has announced that he will remain at West Ham United, a decision that comes as a relief to the club and its fans. The England international’s future had been uncertain since the Hammers’ relegation to the Championship on the final day of the season. Despite the setback, Bowen has chosen to stay and lead the team through this challenging period.

item.title: How have missed targets affected Newcastle's summer rebuild?
item.description:
The Unseen Struggle of Newcastle’s Summer Rebuild

Newcastle United’s summer transfer window has been a tale of missed targets, with the club’s efforts to secure top talent falling short. While the Magpies have managed to land a handful of promising young players, the failure to sign Johan Manzambi, Victor Munoz, and Hugo Ekitike, among others, has left a sense of uncertainty hanging over the club.

The fact that these players have opted for other Premier League clubs, such as Aston Villa, Liverpool, and Manchester United, highlights the intense competition for top talent in the English topflight. Manzambi’s decision to join Villa, for instance, was likely swayed by the prospect of Champions League football, which Newcastle cannot offer this season.

item.title: Trump Promised Proof of Election Tampering. His Document Release Fell Far Short.
item.description:
The Promise Unfulfilled

President Trump’s long-awaited release of documents purporting to prove widespread election tampering had been eagerly anticipated by his supporters and detractors alike. The President had repeatedly claimed that the evidence would be conclusive, a smoking gun that would finally vindicate his repeated assertions of a stolen election. But when the documents were finally made public, they failed to meet the lofty expectations that had been set.

The stark reality was that the documents released by the Trump administration were largely routine and unremarkable, a collection of mostly benign communications and procedural notes that offered no tangible proof of the widespread election sabotage that the President had claimed to have uncovered. In fact, a closer examination of the documents revealed that they were frequently mundane and lacked any clear connection to the President’s claims of electoral malfeasance. The absence of concrete evidence was all the more striking given the President’s earlier boasts that the released documents would be “very big” and would “show everyone” the extent of the election tampering.

item.title: World Cup final ref confirmed: Who is the Spain vs Argentina official?
item.description:
World Cup Showdown: Slovenian Referee Ready for Spain vs Argentina Final

The stage is set for a thrilling conclusion to the World Cup, with Spain and Argentina set to clash in the final at New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday. item.title: Warnock and Ossoff, Georgia’s Senators, Ridicule Trump’s Election Fraud Claims
item.description:
Georgia’s Senators Stand Firm Against Trump’s Election Fraud Claims

In a state where the 2020 presidential election was a hotly contested battleground, two of Georgia’s senators are pushing back against former President Donald Trump’s persistent claims of widespread election fraud. Senators Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff, both Democrats, have joined forces to ridicule Trump’s assertions, calling them a baseless attempt to undermine the integrity of the electoral process.

The senators’ remarks come as no surprise, given the overwhelming evidence of a smooth and secure election in Georgia. In a statement, Warnock said, “The facts are clear: the 2020 Senate election in Georgia was a long-settled issue, and we’ve moved on from the conspiracy theories that plagued our state during the presidential election.” Ossoff echoed Warnock’s sentiments, stating that the state’s election officials had worked tirelessly to ensure the integrity of the vote.

item.title: Trump revives claims of election interference during address to nation
item.description:
The former US president Donald Trump made claims of election interference during a speech to a Republican Party event in Ohio on Saturday night, reviving allegations he raised in the wake of the 2020 presidential election.

Mr. Trump’s speech was a thinly veiled attempt to whip up support for a slate of Republican candidates running in next month’s primary election. The former president used the event to endorse several of the candidates, and also to deliver a broadside against the current administration, which he portrayed as weak and ineffective.

item.title: ‘We are waiting with bated breath’: gathering El Niño could be the strongest on record, BoM says
item.description:
Unprecedented Heat: El Niño’s Potential Impacts on a Scorching Planet

The Pacific Ocean is stirring, and the consequences could be catastrophic. Australia’s Bureau of Meteorology warns that the gathering El Niño could be the strongest on record, with potential implications for global temperatures. As the world holds its breath, experts are sounding the alarm, and the scientific community is scrambling to understand the magnitude of this phenomenon.

Climate models are painting a dire picture, with forecasts suggesting that the El Niño could peak between +2.2°C and above +3°C in the Niño 3.4 region of the equatorial Pacific. Dr. Zhi-Weng Chua, a senior climatologist at the Bureau of Meteorology, notes that this would be a remarkable event, with a chance it could rank as the highest on record. The bureau’s own model has the El Niño peaking at about +3.3°C, with the phenomenon staying in place until at least the coming summer.

item.title: Former Italian motorway chief sentenced over bridge collapse
item.description:
A Legacy of Failure

The once-majestic Genoa motorway bridge, a symbol of Italy’s engineering prowess, lay in ruins on a sweltering summer evening in 2018. The catastrophic collapse claimed the lives of 43 people, leaving a trail of devastation and heartbreak in its wake. Today, the former CEO of Italy’s main highway operator, Giovanni Castellucci, has been held accountable for the tragedy, sentencing him to 12 years in prison. The verdict sends a stark message that those responsible for the disaster will be brought to justice.

item.title: Mamdani Urges New Yorkers to Stay Indoors Because of Wildfire Smoke
item.description:
Toxic Skies: New York City Braces for Wildfire Smoke

As a thick layer of wildfire smoke blankets the city, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has issued a stark warning to the residents of New York: stay indoors. The unprecedented advisory, issued in response to a growing air quality crisis, is a stark reminder of the far-reaching consequences of climate change.

In a city already reeling from the effects of heatwaves and storms, the sudden influx of wildfire smoke has brought a new and unpredictable threat. With air quality indices soaring to hazardous levels, the risks to public health are undeniable. Every New Yorker should take precautions, Mayor Mamdani urged, emphasizing the importance of taking immediate action to mitigate the risks.

item.title: National Academies Report Backs Climate Change Attribution Science
item.description:
A Leap Forward in Climate Accountability

A landmark report from the National Academies has given a significant boost to the field of climate change attribution science, a crucial tool in holding polluters accountable for the devastating effects of global warming. The report’s findings have major implications for lawsuits seeking damages for severe events exacerbated by climate change, which are increasingly becoming a key strategy in the fight against climate inaction.

item.title: Police foil kidnap plot, arrest two foreign suspects
item.description:

item.title: What Can We Learn From Burning Down This House?
item.description:
Blazing the Way to Resilience

Deep within the charred remains of a once-thriving community lies a crucial lesson in the face of intensifying wildfires: that even in the midst of devastation, innovation can spark new hope. As our climate correspondent Mira Rojanasakul delves into the unconventional world of a lab pioneering the protection of homes from the relentless flames, a narrative of resilience emerges, underscored by the sobering reality that the window for action is rapidly closing.

item.title: Inflation Respite Gives More Consumers a Chance to Spend
item.description:
A Fragile Reprieve: Consumers Breathe Easier, but Inflation’s Grip Remains Tense

A welcome respite from the relentless march of inflation has given millions of consumers a rare chance to catch their breath and replenish their depleted wallets. The temporary reprieve, courtesy of lower gas prices, has sparked a surge in discretionary spending, a trend that is being closely watched by economists and policymakers worldwide. However, the fragile nature of this reprieve has left many wondering how long it will last, as gas prices begin to creep higher again, threatening to undo the modest gains made in recent months.

item.title: Kenya: Ruto’s cash handouts fuel 2027 vote-buying fears
item.description:
A Culture of Handouts: Kenya’s 2027 Election Landscape Shifts

Kenya’s electoral landscape is undergoing a seismic shift, driven by a stark reality: the proliferation of cash handouts. item.title: British Steel is taken into public ownership to save UK supply
item.description:
Britain Takes Control of Vital Steelworks to Secure National Supply

In a move hailed as crucial to Britain’s industrial strength, the Labour government has formally taken British Steel into public ownership, expropriating it from its Chinese owner, Jingye. This decisive action, 15 months in the making, aims to safeguard the future of steel making in the UK, protect skilled jobs, and ensure a vital national capability.

The takeover was facilitated by the Steel Industry (Nationalisation) Act, which received Royal Assent on Wednesday, enabling the government to step in and prevent the closure of the Scunthorpe steelworks, which had threatened to shut down in April last year. The facility, Britain’s last remaining producer of primary steel from iron ore, was on the brink of collapse after its Chinese owner, Jingye, indicated its intention to walk away from the business.

item.title: Wales pick Lake against Boks after injury scare

item.title: Canada Wildfire Air Pollution and Heat Wave Combo Pose Heightened Health Risks

item.description:
